subject.title: Feature: Add denylist support for exec-approvals

question: Should a deny-pattern match force a human one-shot approval across both gateway and node exec hosts, or be an unconditional hard denial?
rationale: This changes the execution trust boundary and persisted policy semantics under permissive full/off settings; choosing approval versus hard denial requires explicit maintainer security intent.

options.title: Human approval overlay
options.body: A deny match overrides automatic allow and durable trust, then requires an explicit one-shot human decision consistently on both hosts.

options.title: Unconditional hard denial
options.body: A deny match always blocks execution, simplifying enforcement but removing any exceptional approval path.

options.title: No native policy
options.body: Keep core allowlist-only and rely on external policy plugins, leaving native gateway/node exec behavior without deny-over-allow control.

recommendation.title: Human approval overlay
recommendation.body: A deny match overrides automatic allow and durable trust, then requires an explicit one-shot human decision consistently on both hosts.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has direct recent involvement in scoping the native policy and is the strongest history-backed owner for the security-boundary decision.
